chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ibn Faddal, from Ghalib ibn Uthman, from Rawh ibn Abd al-Rahim, who said:

Abu Abd Allah عليه السلام urinated while I was standing by his head, and I had with me a small water vessel—or he said: a jug. When the stream of urine stopped, he gestured with his hand, saying, "Like this, to me," so I handed him the water, and he performed wudu (ablution) in that very place.

key_terms.إِدَاوَةٌ: a small water vessel used for carrying water
key_terms.شَخْبُ الْبَوْلِ: the stream or flow of urine
key_terms.مَكَانَهُ: in his place; right there where he was
key_terms.هَكَذَا إِلَيَّ: like this, to me; a gesture requesting that the water be handed over

ai.seo_question: How did Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام perform wudu (ablution) after urination according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates that Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام, after finishing urination, requested water and then performed wudu (ablution) immediately in that place. It relates to the etiquettes and practical conduct surrounding states that necessitate taharah (ritual purity).
